concept.title: Migration prerequisites
concept.abstract: This section explains the prerequisites for successful Markdown-to-DITA migration, including source file requirements, repository structure, metadata consistency, and Markdown authoring standards. The AI Agent learns how to assess conversion readiness, identify potential migration issues, and recognize content that may require custom converter configuration or review.

conbody.p:
Before submitting the Markdown source to the Markdown to DITA converter, verify the following prerequisites are met:
All content for migration is in plain-text Markdown files (.md/.markdown), not mixed with binary formats.
Files use standard Markdown syntax for headings, lists, links, images, code blocks, and tables.
Repository structure (folders and file names) is stable and reflects logical groupings (e.g., user-guide/, admin/, api/).
Metadata is used consistently across files if you expect it to become DITA metadata.
conbody.note: If your Markdown uses raw HTML or custom extensions such as Sphinx roles, MkDocs admonitions, GitHub-style callouts, share syntax samples with the DITA architecture team so the Markdown converter configuration can be customized.
